headline: Netanyahu publishes 10-point national security doctrine (preemptive strikes, border buffer zones) 9 days before Oct 27 election
dek: Netanyahu unveiled a new 3-page, 10-principle national security doctrine on the government website Sunday: preemptive strikes against perceived threats, buffer zones along borders (locations unspecified), domestic arms production, AI/quantum, illegal settlement expansion across 'Land of Israel'.…
sources: Israeli government official website (doctrine document); JPost, TRT World/Reuters, Anadolu Agency, Times of India
fault_line: Security doctrine or campaign stunt — will Israel's next government inherit a preemptive-war mandate?

sections.what_happened: Netanyahu unveiled a new 3-page, 10-principle national security doctrine on the government website Sunday: preemptive strikes against perceived threats, buffer zones along borders (locations unspecified), domestic arms production, AI/quantum, illegal settlement expansion across 'Land of Israel'. Claims Gaza/Lebanon/Yemen/Iran offensives dismantled Iranian encirclement and removed 'nuclear annihilation' threat. Opposition leader Lapid called it 'superficial'/'bizarre' ('looks like it was drafted by the free version of an AI chatbot'); Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar) dismissed it as 'empty pages filled with slogans' and accused Netanyahu of exploiting fear. Meanwhile: anti-draft protests erupted (JPost Oct 18, Eisenkot leading Netanyahu in polls); mass anti-Netanyahu protests at Tel Aviv Habima Square less than two weeks before Oct 27 vote (TOI); Brothers and Sisters in Arms threaten suit against Likud lawyer over election-interference accusations (Haaretz Oct 13); Arab parties seek record turnout, could hold balance of power (Business Standard Oct 18); 50k+ diaspora Israelis flying home to vote (FAF Oct 18).
sections.what_verified: TRT World (Reuters-sourced, Oct 19), Anadolu Agency (Oct 19), JPost podcast headlines (Oct 18 14:05), Times of India video (weekend Habima protests), Haaretz (Oct 13), Business Standard (Oct 18), FAF (Oct 18).
sections.what_disputed: Netanyahu's claim that offensives 'dismantled Iranian encirclement' is his campaign framing — carried as attributed; Iran-war outcome claims remain contested; themunicheye 'mass protests' piece mixes stale Ronen Bar-dismissal content — NOT used as source.
sections.why_matters: Nine days before Israelis vote, Netanyahu has published a doctrine that makes preemptive strikes official policy — and the streets are answering. The election is now a referendum on whether Israel's next wars are already written.
sections.context: Background: Israel — NEW: Netanyahu publishes 10-point national security doctrine (preemptive strikes, border buffer zones) 9 days before Oct 27 election; anti-draft and anti-Netanyahu protests erupt; Eisenkot leads Netanyahu in polls; opposition calls doctrine 'empty slogans'; Arab parties push record turnout

totw_analysis: Our read: Nine days before Israelis vote, Netanyahu has published a doctrine that makes preemptive strikes official policy — and the streets are answering. The election is now a referendum on whether Israel's next wars are already written. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Security doctrine or campaign stunt — will Israel's next government inherit a preemptive-war mandate?
